title: Vocabulary: describing trends and comparisons for Writing Task 1
status: Owner approved v1.0.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Learners can read the axes of a line graph and a bar chart.
Optional vocabulary lesson: use when Task 1 answers repeat 'increase' and 'decrease' or describe changes inaccurately.

objectives.text: Use precise verbs, nouns and adverbs for trends (plummet, level off, a steady rise, marginally) with accurate grammar.
Compare figures accurately with proportion and comparison language (twice as many, account for, overtake, by contrast).
Match the strength of a word to the size of the change, so that descriptions are accurate, not just varied.

levels.foundation: Use the verb + adverb pattern only (rose sharply, fell slightly) and the word bank during writing.
levels.core: Use at least two noun patterns (a sharp rise in ...) and two comparison phrases accurately in the paragraph.
levels.extension: Write one sentence that combines a trend and a comparison (for example: '..., overtaking gas in about 2016').
levels.high_band: Write the full overview and both body paragraphs with no repeated trend word and every number supporting a key feature.

word_bank.example: Wind and solar power rose steadily.
The use of coal declined sharply after 2005.

word_bank.meaning: fall / rise very fast by a large amount
word_bank.example: Sales soared from 5% to 40% in two years.

word_bank.meaning: stop changing and stay at about the same level
word_bank.example: Gas remained stable at about a third.

word_bank.item: peak at / reach a peak of

word_bank.meaning: noun pattern for trends with an adjective
word_bank.example: There was a sharp fall in coal use.

word_bank.meaning: adverbs showing speed or size of change
be a particular proportion of a total
word_bank.example: Coal accounted for 58% of electricity in 2000.

word_bank.meaning: become larger than something that was larger before

word_bank.example: Teenagers spent three times as many hours on social media.

word_bank.meaning: introduce a different or opposite trend

word_bank.item: approximately / just over / just under / nearly
word_bank.meaning: give a number that is not exact
part of a total, usually a percentage
word_bank.example: The share of gas changed very little.

stages.title: Opening challenge: varied or accurate?
stages.student: Decide which sentence describes the graph best before the reveal.
stages.teacher: Show the graph. Learners vote. Reveal the comments.
stages.say: A word must fit the size of the change. Variety comes second.
stages.check: Learners can say why 'plummeted' is wrong for gas.

stages.title: Word bank: verbs, nouns and adverbs
stages.student: Sort the word bank into 'up', 'down', 'no change' and 'compare'. Mark how strong each word is.
stages.teacher: Board a scale from 'slightly' to 'dramatically'. Drill the two patterns: verb + adverb, adjective + noun + in.
stages.say: Two patterns: 'rose sharply' and 'a sharp rise in'.
stages.check: Learners transform three sentences between the two patterns.

stages.title: Describe the graph accurately
stages.student: Complete each sentence with ONE word that matches the graph.
stages.teacher: Eight minutes. During the reveal, accept alternatives only if the size of change fits.
stages.say: Check the numbers before you choose the word.
stages.check: Most learners score six or more.

stages.title: Spot the inaccurate description
stages.student: Choose the accurate sentence each time.
stages.teacher: Focus on comparison maths: twice as many, nearly half, overtook.
stages.say: Examiners check accuracy; wrong comparisons lose marks.
stages.check: Learners explain each wrong option with a number.

stages.title: Plan your paragraph
stages.student: Choose the three key features and the words you will use for each.
stages.teacher: Check plans quickly: one overview feature must be a comparison.
stages.say: Plan the features, then choose the words.
stages.check: Every learner has three features noted.

stages.title: Write independently
stages.student: Write an overview and one body paragraph, using at least six word-bank items accurately.
stages.teacher: Twelve minutes, no model visible. Note learners using the bank.
stages.say: Tick each word-bank item as you use it.

stages.title: Compare with the model
stages.student: Underline the trend words in the model and check your own paragraph with the checklist.
stages.teacher: Ask: which word in the model is strongest, and is it justified by the numbers?
stages.say: The model is illustrative, not a target band.
stages.check: Learners correct one inaccurate word in their own text.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the homework.
stages.say: Use the noun pattern at least once in every Task 1 answer.
stages.check: Every learner writes one noun-pattern sentence from memory.

blocks.title: Varied or accurate?
blocks.mode: Opening challenge; learners decide before the reveal
blocks.instructions: In one country, the share of electricity generated from gas rose from 30% to 32% between 2000 and 2020. Three learners described this change. Which sentence is best?

examples.label: Learner A
examples.text: The use of gas soared over the period.
examples.comment: Inaccurate: 'soared' means a very large, fast rise. Two percentage points is tiny.

examples.label: Learner B
examples.text: Gas remained relatively stable, rising only marginally from 30% to 32%.
examples.comment: Best: the words match the size of the change and the numbers prove it.

examples.label: Learner C
examples.comment: Inaccurate: the line barely moves; 'dramatically' exaggerates.

blocks.title: Describe the graph accurately
blocks.mode: Controlled practice; word bank open for foundation only
blocks.instructions: Look at the graph. Complete each sentence with ONE word that describes the data accurately.

figure.title: Electricity generated from three sources, one country, 2000-2020
figure.alt: Line graph of three sources of electricity from 2000 to 2020. Coal is stable at about 58 then falls sharply to 22. Gas stays between 30 and 33. Wind and solar rise from 2 to 41, overtaking gas around 2016 and coal around 2017.

items.prompt: Between 2010 and 2020, the share of coal fell ______, from 49% to 22%.
items.reason: A large, fast fall; dramatically or considerably also fit.

items.prompt: Gas remained ______ at around a third throughout the period.
Wind and solar power ______ coal in about 2017.
items.reason: One source became larger than the other.

items.prompt: In 2000, coal ______ for 58% of all electricity.
There was a ______ rise in wind and solar power after 2010.
Gas use rose only ______, from 30% to 32%.
Between 2000 and 2005, coal changed very little, ______ wind and solar doubled.
By 2020, wind and solar produced ______ under half of the country's electricity.

blocks.title: Spot the inaccurate description
blocks.instructions: Look at the bar chart. Choose the sentence, A, B or C, that describes the data accurately.

figure.title: Average weekly hours spent on four activities by teenagers, one city, 2010 and 2020
figure.alt: Bar chart comparing 2010 and 2020. Social media rises from 6 to 18 hours. Sport falls from 8 to 6. Reading falls from 5 to 3. Homework stays at 10.

items.prompt: Social media
options: A  Time on social media doubled between 2010 and 2020.
B  Teenagers spent three times as long on social media in 2020 as in 2010.
C  Time on social media rose slightly.

items.prompt: Homework
options: A  Time spent on homework remained unchanged at ten hours.
B  Homework peaked at ten hours in 2020.
C  Homework fluctuated around ten hours.

items.prompt: Reading
items.reason: A fall of two hours; reading was the lowest activity in 2020.
options: A  Reading plummeted to zero.
B  Reading overtook sport in 2020.
C  Reading fell from five to three hours, the lowest figure in 2020.

items.prompt: Sport and social media in 2010
items.reason: Sport was higher in 2010; social media overtook it by 2020.
options: A  In 2010, teenagers spent more time on social media than on sport.
B  Social media overtook sport between 2010 and 2020.
C  Sport and social media accounted for the same time in both years.

items.prompt: Overall
items.evidence: Only social media rose; sport and reading fell; homework unchanged
items.reason: A identifies the main feature without false detail.
options: A  Overall, social media was the only activity to grow, while time spent on sport and reading declined.
B  Overall, teenagers spent less time on every activity.
C  Overall, homework rose more than any other activity.

blocks.title: Overview and one body paragraph
blocks.mode: Independent classroom application after modelling; not a full Task 1 or Writing Screener
blocks.prompt: The graph shows the percentage of electricity generated from three sources in one country between 2000 and 2020. Write an overview and ONE body paragraph (about 90-110 words) describing the most important changes.

figure.title: Electricity generated from three sources, one country, 2000-2020
figure.alt: Line graph of three sources of electricity from 2000 to 2020. Coal is stable at about 58 then falls sharply to 22. Gas stays between 30 and 33. Wind and solar rise from 2 to 41, overtaking gas around 2016 and coal around 2017.

blocks.conditions: 12 minutes, independent. No model visible. Record word-bank use.
blocks.support: Overview frame: Overall, ... while ... . Body: start with the biggest change; use one verb + adverb pattern and one adjective + noun pattern; add one comparison.
blocks.high_band: No trend word may be repeated; every number must support a key feature.
blocks.model_label: Illustrative classroom model for discussion only. Not a certified band answer.
blocks.model:
Overall, electricity generation shifted from coal towards wind and solar power, which had become the largest source by the end of the period, while the share of gas remained relatively stable.

In 2000, coal accounted for 58% of electricity, but after 2005 its share plummeted, reaching just 22% in 2020. By contrast, wind and solar power, which produced a mere 2% at the start, grew slowly at first and then soared after 2010, overtaking coal between 2015 and 2020 and climbing to 41%. Gas, meanwhile, rose only marginally, from 30% to a peak of 33% before levelling off.
checklist: Lexical Resource: Does each trend word match the size of the change?
Lexical Resource: Have you used both a verb + adverb and an adjective + noun pattern?
Task Achievement: Does the overview give the main trends without numbers?
Grammatical Range and Accuracy: Are past tenses and prepositions (from ... to, by, at) correct?

blocks.title: Homework: transform the pattern
blocks.mode: Homework; checked at the start of the next lesson
blocks.instructions: Rewrite each sentence using the noun pattern. Write the missing word (ONE word).

items.prompt: Prices rose slightly. → There was a ______ rise in prices.
Sales fell dramatically. → There was a dramatic ______ in sales.
Visitor numbers grew steadily. → There was a steady ______ in visitor numbers.
Unemployment fluctuated. → Unemployment showed some ______.
Car sales peaked at 2 million. → Car sales reached a ______ of 2 million.
Exports increased considerably. → There was a ______ increase in exports.

exit_ticket: Two ways to say 'went down a lot':
The word I use for a very small change:

blocks.title: Fresh check: museum visitors
blocks.instructions: Look at the graph. Complete each sentence with ONE word, or choose the correct letter.

figure.title: Annual visitors to three museums, one city, 2014-2022 (thousands)
figure.alt: Line graph of three museums from 2014 to 2022. All three drop sharply in 2020. The science museum is highest except in 2020. The art gallery rises from 200 to 310, falls to 120 in 2020, then reaches 330 in 2022. The history museum stays near 150 apart from 2020.

items.prompt: In 2020, visitor numbers at all three museums ______ dramatically.
Apart from 2020, the history museum remained relatively ______ at around 150,000.
The art gallery ______ at 330,000 visitors in 2022.
Which sentence is accurate?
options: A  In 2014, the art gallery had more visitors than the science museum.
B  In 2014, the science museum had three times as many visitors as the art gallery.
C  In 2014, the science museum had just over twice as many visitors as the art gallery.

items.prompt: Which sentence is accurate?
options: A  Between 2014 and 2018, the art gallery saw a steady rise in visitors.
B  Between 2014 and 2018, the art gallery fluctuated wildly.
C  Between 2014 and 2018, the art gallery overtook the science museum.

items.prompt: In 2022, the art gallery ______ the history museum by a wide margin, but not the science museum.
